judged_text: evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar was set to null two lines earlier, dropping all team-host destination calendars for collective bookings whose organizer has no destination calendar. For a COLLECTIVE event type with no eventType-level destinationCalendar and an organizer without one, team members' calendars are silently discarded and events are created on none of the team hosts' calendars — the exact collective-multi-host case this PR claims to fix.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exist (`destinationCalendar: ... : null,` around the `evt` construction). A few lines later, for COLLECTIVE team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional-chained `push` is a silent no-op, so `teamDestinationCalendars` never get added. This matches the finding’s scenario (collective booking where organizer has no destination calendar and no eventType-level destination calendar), causing team members’ destination calendars to be dropped.
